subject: On-prem deployment: license boundary & conditional fallback controls
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Akhil Singh <akhil@healthgrid.com>
Cc: David Kim <david@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: On-prem deployment: license boundary & conditional fallback controls

Hi Akhil —

Thanks again for the product walkthrough yesterday. Per our procurement checklist, I'm attaching our initial redline of the MSA + proposed Order Form exhibits for the on-prem (VPC) deployment. A few items we want to clarify up front so your team can route internally: 

- License boundary: the drafting team asked whether HealthGrid will require a "licensed runtime" clause that allows you to snapshot and run model binaries in your environment for disaster recovery. If you need that, please confirm whether the snapshot/window should be limited to a witness-only access or full operator access.
- Conditional fallback / escape hatch: our engineers proposed an operational fallback clause (see attached) — essentially, when Redwood is unable to serve a pinned model variant for >72 hours, we provide either (a) temporary hosted routing to an agreed compatible model hosted in Redwood (data processed in-region), or (b) delivery of the artifacts for your on-prem execution under an agreed escrow-lite process. We need HealthGrid's preference and acceptable SLAs (RTO window).
- Audit & evidence: procurement asked for a compact list of what evidence you need (SOC2, forensic snapshot, operator witness). If you can send the checklist, we’ll match exhibits.

Attached: HealthGrid_MSA_Redline_v1.pdf — this highlights the clauses above and flags where we think Exhibit G (Operational Handover) will live.

Can you loop in legal/procurement and let me know: (1) whether HealthGrid wants witness-level operator access or witness-only snapshoting; (2) whether 72 hours is acceptable for the fallback trigger; and (3) any procurement timelines to get this into the PO/Order Form?

If it's helpful, David can drop a sample clause into the addendum.

Thanks,

— Marissa Cole
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com
Attachments: HealthGrid_MSA_Redline_v1.pdf (pdf, 423 KB)

From: Akhil Singh <akhil@healthgrid.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: HealthGrid Procurement <procurement@healthgrid.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Oct 2026 08:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem deployment: license boundary & conditional fallback controls

Marissa —

Thanks for the redline and the clear list. Procurement/legal have a few quick points: 

1) Escape hatch — we like the idea of a staged approach but 72 hours may be long for a clinical workload. Can you propose a staggered trigger (e.g., 24/48/72 windows) with specific mitigations per window?

2) Snapshot/control access — HealthGrid prefers witness-only access during snapshoting unless there's a documented forensics/DR activation. Full operator credentials are a last resort and would require insurance + onsite witness.

3) Evidence — see attached procurement checklist. Priority: SOC2 Type II report, recent penetration test summary, and a chain-of-custody statement for any key material (KMS/HSM) used during evidence handover.

We can start legal redlines if Redwood can provide the suggested staggered trigger language and a proposed list of escrow-lite deliverables. Also, please confirm whether hosted fallback (option a) would preserve data locality in our primary US region.

Akhil
Akhil Singh
Senior Counsel, HealthGrid
Attachments: HG_Procurement_Checklist.xlsx (xlsx, 89 KB)

From: David Kim <david@redwoodinference.com>
To: Akhil Singh <akhil@healthgrid.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem deployment: license boundary & conditional fallback controls

Hi Akhil —

Thanks for the checklist. Quick technical clarifications and a proposed drafting snippet below.

On data locality: hosted fallback (option a) will run in the same AWS region you specify for the VPC deployment; we can narrow to us-west-2 if you need. It will not route outside the agreed geography.

On staggered triggers: below is a suggested set of windows and mitigations — please consider as starting text for the addendum.

--- Proposed Addendum Snippet (for redlines / legal) ---
"In the event Redwood is unable to serve the primary pinned model variant to Customer requests due to platform capacity or infrastructure outage, the following remedial stages will apply: (a) 0-24 hours: Redwood shall notify Customer and enable transparent hosted routing to a compatible model variant within the same region; (b) 24-48 hours: Redwood shall provision a prioritized capacity pool (burst) and make available temporary API endpoints; (c) 48+ hours: If service continuity is not restored within 48 hours, Redwood will provide either (i) escrow-lite delivery of minimal artifacts necessary to run the agreed model locally (forensics snapshot plus runtime image), or (ii) a mutually-agreed on-prem operator access window under supervised witness conditions. Escrow-lite deliverables exclude any third-party licensed tooling. Customer shall be responsible for local infrastructure and observed operator controls."
--- end snippet ---

On operator witness/sample: our standard approach is to deliver a sealed snapshot and a signed manifest (hashes + manifest of key materials). For on-prem operator access we propose a short, scheduled witness window (max 8 hours) with pre-agreed playbook and audit log streaming.

I've attached a draft Exhibit G (priv-deploy-exhibit-draft.docx) that maps deliverables to the windows above. If legal wants different timing (e.g., 24 vs 48), we can update.

Thanks,

— David
David Kim
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: priv-deploy-exhibit-draft.docx (docx, 57 KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Akhil Singh <akhil@healthgrid.com>
Cc: David Kim <david@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwoodinference.com>, HealthGrid Procurement <procurement@healthgrid.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Oct 2026 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem deployment: license boundary & conditional fallback controls

Akhil / team —

Appreciate the quick turn. To keep procurement moving, our proposal is: accept the staggered 0/24/48 windows but we will flag the 48+ as the point where escrow-lite or operator-access options are available. David's draft Exhibit G maps exactly what we will hand over in the escrow-lite path.

Next steps: 
- Akhil / procurement to confirm witness-only vs operator access policy in writing (we've noted HealthGrid prefers witness-only unless DR is invoked).
- Soojin, can Redwood legal pencil in language that preserves Redwood's right to exclude third-party licensed tools from the deliverables (per David's note)?
- Akhil, if procurement can circulate any mandatory insurance or on-site requirements, we'll slot that into the Order Form.

I'll upload the annotated redline (attached) to the deal in HubSpot and route for DocuSign once legal signs off. Proposed internal timeline: redline turn by Fri 10/9, PO execution by 10/20.

Thanks — Marissa
Attachments: redlines_with_comments.pdf (pdf, 210 KB)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Akhil Singh <akhil@healthgrid.com>
Cc: David Kim <david@redwoodinference.com>, HealthGrid Procurement <procurement@healthgrid.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Oct 2026 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem deployment: license boundary & conditional fallback controls

Hi all —

I've reviewed David's proposed snippet and the redline. My high-level legal notes: 

1) Trigger timing: We are willing to accept a staggered 0/24/48 approach but recommend changing the 48+ trigger language to require a formal "Escalation Notice" (72 hours after initial notification) before Redwood must commence escrow-lite artifact delivery. This provides a narrow administrative buffer to validate the outage and avoids accidental early artifact handover. Open to HealthGrid shortening that buffer with additional SLA credits.

2) Third-party tooling: we will keep the carve-out excluding third-party licensed tooling from deliverables, but will include a commitment to provide interface-level descriptors and, where possible, containerized runtimes that do not contain third-party binaries.

3) Operator access: propose firm constraints — an 8-hour supervised window, mutual nondisclosure for any operator actions, and a requirement that HealthGrid's witness team be present (on-site or via recorded video). We will require a brief pre-access runbook to be exchanged 48 hours prior.

4) Evidence package: Redwood will provide SOC2 Type II, recent pentest summary, manifest + signed hashes for any snapshot, and a chain-of-custody form. We cannot provide HSM key material; instead we will provide KMS public key fingerprints and attestations.

If HealthGrid wants a tighter Escrow Notice (e.g., 48 hours), we can negotiate commercial credits in the Order Form.

I'm placing a DocuSign skeleton in the HubSpot deal (link below) with the draft Exhibit G attached for ease of review. Please let me know final choices and we can produce a redline for signature.
